title: Hellfire Ramparts
body: The Hellfire Ramparts are the battlements on the outer face of Hellfire Citadel, the first of its defenses that any attacker from the peninsula must climb. The Fel Horde holds them in strength. Bonechewer destroyers and hungerers walk the walls, Bleeding Hollow archers, scryers and darkcasters stand among them, and Shattered Hand warhounds wait for their beastmaster to loose them. The officers warn their sentries to keep a close watch, for intruders could come at any time. Watchkeeper Gargolmar commands the watch with his own subordinates at his side, the demon Omor the Unscarred holds a stretch of the walls, and at the far end a rider called Vazruden the Herald circles above the battlement on his drake, Nazan. Honor Hold and Thrallmar, caught between the citadel and the Burning Legion, mean to strike at the fortress now, and the key to it is breaking through these walls first.

title: Watchkeeper Gargolmar
body: Watchkeeper Gargolmar commands the watch on the Hellfire Ramparts, and he trusts his nose as much as his eyes. When strangers set foot on the walls he scents them at once, warning his soldiers that fresh meat has somehow breached the citadel and that they should be wary. He does not fight alone. The Hellfire Watchers, his own subordinates, stand close by, and they are expected to heal him the moment he calls. He relishes the work, promising each foe that this may hurt a little.

parts.body: Gargolmar called on his watchers to heal him and drove back any who pressed too close, but the watch on the ramparts was broken all the same. He died much as he had fought, laughing at his foes until a cough cut the laugh short.

title: Omor the Unscarred
body: Omor the Unscarred is no orc. He is a demon standing among the fel orcs on the Hellfire Ramparts, and his very name boasts that he bears no scar. He meets intruders with scorn, demanding to know who dares stand against him and promising that their insolence will be their death. He calls up fiendish hounds to fight at his side, urging each to feast and eat its fill, and lays curses on those who face him, spitting words of power as he does.

parts.body: Omor fell on the ramparts all the same, for all his boasting. His last words were no plea but a warning, gasped out as he died: it is not over. Whatever he meant by it, the stretch of wall he had guarded stood open.

title: Vazruden the Herald
body: Vazruden the Herald guards the far end of the Hellfire Ramparts, circling above it on the back of his drake, Nazan, while sentries hold the battlement below. When the sentries fall he comes down to meet the intruders himself, mocking them for facing so many challenges in vain and promising that soon their people will kneel to his lord. Whose herald he is, he does not say. At most he boasts in the fight of a higher call he answers, or of a dark lord who laughs at those who stand against him.

parts.body: Vazruden fought on foot while Nazan wheeled overhead and rained fire on the stones. When the herald was hard pressed he called for the drake to come down and fight beside him, and still it did not save him. With his dying breath he swore that his lord would be the end of them all.

title: Weaken the Ramparts
body: Thrallmar and Honor Hold are caught between two enemies, Hellfire Citadel to the west and the Burning Legion to the east. For now the Legion's attention is turned toward the Dark Portal, and both outposts mean to use that moment to strike at the fel orcs of the citadel, beginning with its ramparts. In Honor Hold, Lieutenant Chadwick sends volunteers up onto the walls with proof to be brought to Gunny across the hall; in Thrallmar, Stone Guard Stok'ton does the same, with Caza'rez awaiting the report. The targets are the leaders of the walls: Watchkeeper Gargolmar, Omor the Unscarred and the drake Nazan, whose hand, hoof and head are the proof required.

parts.body: With the three dead, the defenders of the ramparts were thrown into disarray, and the artillery on the walls fell silent, so that an army could come close enough to strike at the citadel itself. Yet at both outposts the one who took the report sensed there was more to the citadel than met the eye, and held a further task in reserve.

title: The Herald's Letter
body: On the body of Vazruden the Herald lies a rolled letter, its seal still unbroken and marked with an elaborate I in blood-red ink. Whoever cracks it open finds a message disturbing enough to carry straight back to the commanders of the peninsula, Force Commander Danath Trollbane at Honor Hold or Nazgrel at Thrallmar. Until now the fel orcs of the citadel have seemed to answer to no one but Kargath Bladefist, their self-styled warchief, and Alliance and Horde alike have fought them as a new Fel Horde risen from nowhere. Yet the herald boasted on the ramparts that soon their people would kneel to his lord.

parts.body: The letter was signed by Illidan. The commander read it twice and was silent a moment before speaking: this was ominous news, and the plans against Hellfire Citadel and its Blood Furnace had to move faster now. The one who had brought the letter was put at the head of them, with the warning that the next mission would be far deadlier than the first.
